257	    """One lazily-built SQLAlchemy engine with an idempotent dispose (#427).
258	
259	    ``factory`` builds the engine on first :meth:`get` (the runner's URL /

262	    one auth handshake per run. :meth:`close` disposes the pool and resets, so
263	    a closed holder lazily rebuilds if reused — never a bricked runner.

266	    def __init__(self, factory: Callable[[], Any]) -> None:
267	        self._factory = factory
268	        self._engine: Any | None = None
269	
270	    def get(self) -> Any:
271	        if self._engine is None:
272	            self._engine = self._factory()
273	        return self._engine
274	
275	    def close(self) -> None:
276	        if self._engine is not None:
277	            self._engine.dispose()
278	            self._engine = None

    full_line_comments = []
    for t in toks:

    blocks, cur = [], []
    for t in full_line_comments:
        if cur and t.start[0] == cur[-1].start[0] + 1 and t.start[1] == cur[-1].start[1]:

        else:

    for blk in blocks:

        if any(DIRECTIVE.search(t.string) or BANNER.search(t.string) for t in blk): continue

        text = " ".join(t.string.lstrip("#:").lstrip("#").strip() for t in blk)

# prebuilt UI image works same-origin without Azure Static Web App "linking"
# (the no-clone `docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up` path — #472).

# This is a TEMPLATE: the nginx image's entrypoint runs envsubst over
# /etc/nginx/templates/*.template at startup, so ${DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM} is filled
# from the env (default http://api:8000, set in frontend/Dockerfile; overridable
# in compose). Only env vars that are actually set are substituted, so nginx's
# own $uri / $host / $scheme runtime vars are left untouched.

# The client-facing scheme, forwarded upstream (#1138). NOT `$scheme`.
#
# This container never terminates TLS — it listens on plain HTTP :8080 and the
# edge in front of it (Azure Container Apps' Envoy ingress, or whatever proxy a
# BYO deployment puts there) does. So `$scheme` here is *deterministically*
# `http` on every request, including ones the browser made over HTTPS. Sending
# `X-Forwarded-Proto: $scheme` doesn't merely lose information — `proxy_set_header`
# REPLACES the edge's correct `https` with our wrong `http`, so the API sees a
# plaintext request and marks the OTP session cookie **without `Secure`** on a
# live HTTPS deployment (ADR 0032; the backend's `_cookie_secure()` infers from
# exactly this header).
#
# So: prefer what the edge told us, and fall back to `$scheme` only when there is
# no edge header at all — the direct-connection case (compose, `docker run -p
# 8080`), where `$scheme` genuinely IS the client-facing scheme.
#
# Trust boundary, stated plainly: this makes nginx trust an inbound header. That
# is sound *because a client cannot reach this hop directly* — ACA's ingress is
# the only route in, and Envoy sets `X-Forwarded-Proto` itself from the TLS
# state, overwriting whatever the client sent. If you deploy this image with NO
# TLS-terminating proxy in front and expose it straight to the internet, a client
# CAN dictate the value; the only thing it influences is cookie-`Secure`
# inference (it grants no authentication and no authorization), and the
# belt-and-braces answer is to set `AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true` explicitly
# on the API — which stops consulting the header at all.
#
# `map` lives in the `http` context: this template renders into conf.d/, which
# nginx includes inside `http { }`, so a top-level directive here is valid.
